The main takeaway from our work is that
the ice sheet margin was more proximal in central Indiana during MIS 3 than previously assumed and that MIS 3 deposits are more widespread in the region than previously assumed.
glacial-lacustral deposits are not ubiquitous in caves in central Indiana, and that the presence of glacial-lacustine deposits may be related to the proximity of the ice sheet margin.
the Laurentide ice margin in central Indiana during MIS 2 was at a more southerly position than previously thought, with the ice lobe extending to the north and west of the current topography.
